methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study of 922 women from Duke Breast Cancer MRI dataset. Racial comparison (White, Black, Other) with logistic/Cox regression. Missing histology data (29.9%) addressed via MICE. Limitations: single institution, no external validation, limited mortality events, historical cohort (2000-2014).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Observational study examining racial disparities in breast cancer subtypes. Identifies higher TNBC prevalence in Black women but survival differences attenuated after adjustment. Limited direct clinical practice guidance; relevant for healthcare equity research.

reporting_quality.justification: Clear Methods with variable extraction and MICE for missing histology. Results systematically present demographic/clinical characteristics and molecular subtype distributions. Data from publicly available Duke dataset cited.

novelty_literature.justification: Confirms known racial disparities in TNBC prevalence. Longitudinal design adds methodologic contribution but findings align with established literature.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear Methods and Results. Discussion contextualizes within literature on racial disparities. Some repetition in background sections.

key_strengths: Large single-institution cohort with standardized MRI diagnostic pathway
Longitudinal design linking molecular subtype, recurrence, survival in single cohort
Rigorous missing data handling with MICE and sensitivity analysis
key_concerns: Limited mortality events restrict multivariable modeling; median OS not estimable
Single institution historical cohort limits generalizability
No genomic data or mechanistic investigation of racial disparities
Survival differences attenuated after adjustment suggests confounding
chief_reviewer.rationale: Observational cohort confirming known racial disparities in TNBC with limited novelty. Tier 4 appropriate for descriptive equity research.
